claims.text: Fine-tuning large language models on new information not acquired during pre-training can encourage model hallucinations.
Prefix-based universal adversarial perturbations can bypass LLM-based guardrail models even when the adversary has no access to the guardrail model.
Natural Language Inference models used for grounding verification struggle with checks that require reasoning over temporal statements, negation, or quantifiers.
Adversaries can bypass safety filters by decomposing malicious tasks into subtasks and solving benign subtasks with aligned frontier models while solving malicious subtasks with non-aligned models.

evidence.description: The authors cite recent literature showing that fine-tuning LLMs on unfamiliar factual data outside their pre-training distribution promotes hallucinated outputs.
Studies demonstrate a two-step attack constructing universal adversarial prefixes that propagate to the response and effectively undermine LLM guardrails across zero-access threat models.
NLI-based automated checks frequently fail on complex grounding validation tasks involving temporal context comparisons, explicit negation, and quantifier evaluation.
Research shows multi-model attack combinations allow aligned frontier models to assist in malicious objectives undetected because individual subqueries sent to them appear benign.

methodologies.name: Generative AI Risk Management Framework
methodologies.description: A lifecycle management framework for addressing generative AI harms comprising identification, measurement, mitigation across four system layers, and operationalization.

limitations.text: NLI-based guardrail models for grounding checks struggle with performing reasoning that involves temporal statements, negation, or quantifiers.
Current alignment methodologies relying on human feedback become unfeasible for supervising AI systems that achieve superhuman performance.

future_work.text: Developing mechanisms to detect hallucinations in video, speech, and multimodal settings.
Designing scalable differentially private model training techniques applicable to models with billions or trillions of parameters.
Extending Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks to multimodal knowledge bases containing text, images, audio, and video.
